item.title: From Fraud to the Frontlines: Scam Centers Caught in the Cambodia-Thailand Conflict
item.description: In December 2025, Thailand struck Cambodian casino and hotel complexes, which it says were scam centers being used by the military. Though contested, the strikes show how a border dispute and transnational crime have become intertwined.

item.title: New Executive Order Ties U.S. Critical Minerals Security to Global Partnerships
item.description: A new executive order makes international cooperation central to U.S. critical minerals security, targeting processed minerals where China dominates. It pairs allied supply agreements with trade tools—and potential price supports—to reduce vulnerabilities.

item.title: The Costs and Global Trade-Offs of U.S. Military Action Against Venezuela
item.description: U.S. military operations in the Caribbean, now in their sixth month, cost $31 million per day, $3 million of which is unbudgeted. The larger cost is the strategic trade-off in the allocation of military assets: Forces in the Caribbean are not available for other hotspots.

item.title: Opting Out: United States to Stop Engaging with More UN Entities
item.description: Prioritizing and refining the coalitions and organizations an administration engages with makes sense, but budget cuts and an anti-multilateralism philosophy come with risks and mean a broader rupture is likely still on the horizon.

item.title: Why Greenland Could Spur Europe’s Digital Awakening
item.description: U.S. pressure over Greenland is pushing Europe to confront a deeper vulnerability: its dependence on U.S. tech. The result could be a profound shift in cloud, AI, and digital sovereignty across the European Union.

item.title: Trump’s Greenland Ambition Is About U.S. Power, Not Alliances
item.description: Trump's push for Greenland isn't about NATO security—it's about controlling vast sums in rare earth minerals. European appeals to Cold War alliances miss the point of his America First doctrine, which prioritizes U.S. economic gain above all else.

item.title: Japan Poised for Early General Election
item.description: Prime Minister Sanae Takaichi’s plan to dissolve the lower house of the Japanese parliament could give her party a mandate for strong leadership—or it could exacerbate current governance challenges.
